title: Odile and the Horizon
premise: Ansel Vasquez, estranged daughter of a disgraced archaeologist, digs graves for a living and owes money to worse people. When an equinox tide exposes a sea cave on the coast of Puerto Aliso, she finds her father's old survey notes hidden inside — notes pointing to the San Telmo, a wreck the salvage fleet has hunted for decades under expiring concession permits. Racing six tides against Captain Ilsa Reyes's industrial dredge operation, Ansel uncovers that the wreck holds not just gold but proof that the permits were forged on stolen Indigenous land claims. She must choose between selling the find to clear her debt or giving the evidence to the coastal community whose ancestors filled that hold. In the end, Ansel sinks the salvage fleet's claim documents in the cave itself, clears her father's name at the cost of her fortune, and watches the town — not the fleet — claim the horizon.
about_author: Astrid Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent seven years charting coastlines from Baja to Patagonia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who trust tides more than institutions.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Tide
chapters.summary: Ansel Vasquez, digging a grave in Puerto Aliso's cliffside cemetery, is cornered by Marlo Quist, who holds her late mother's debts and gives her until the spring equinox to pay. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: weary defiance — she has nothing but a brass compass her father left and a talent for reading ground.

chapters.title: What the Equinox Uncovered
chapters.summary: A once-a-generation low tide drains a sea cave below the cliffs. Ansel explores it at dawn and finds a waterproofed satchel: her father Tomás's survey charts of the San Telmo wreck, dated the year he vanished. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: shock curdling into hunger — the charts are worth a fortune, or a grave.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ansel deciphers the charts: the wreck lies beyond the reef, accessible only during specific tide windows — six of them before the concession permits expire and the government auction opens the waters to the highest bidder. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic; she needs a boat, a crew, and luck she doesn't own.

chapters.title: The Fleet Comes In
chapters.summary: Captain Ilsa Reyes docks the salvage vessel Corvina with state fanfare, promising jobs and glory. Ansel watches Reyes charm the town and recognizes the permit paperwork being unloaded — paperwork bearing her father's forged signature. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: righteous anger replacing fear.

chapters.title: A Boat Called Mercy
chapters.summary: Ansel bargains with Ferro, a retired fisherman whose boat, Mercy, is mortgaged to the same man who owns her debt. He agrees to run her past the reef if she cuts him in — but warns that Reyes buys loyalty cheap and buries refusals deep. POV: Ferro. Emotional beat: grudging alliance between two proud, broke people.

chapters.title: First Dive, First Blood
chapters.summary: Tide one: Ansel dives the outer shoal and confirms the wreck's mast field — and nearly drowns when someone slashes Mercy's mooring line while she's under. She surfaces to find boot prints and a Reyes fleet tender idling offshore. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into certainty that this is now a fight.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Ansel breaks into the harbormaster's archive and compares the concession permits against her father's real hand: the forgeries are clumsy, and the land claims beneath them belong to the displaced Chumara families of Puerto Aliso. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the personal quest widens into something larger than debt.

chapters.title: Sela of the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Ansel brings the evidence to Sela Chumara, a matriarch who once employed her father and despises him for what he signed. Sela offers testimony but no forgiveness — and reveals Tomás didn't vanish; he was running from Quist and Reyes's predecessor. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: grief and inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Tide Two, Taken
chapters.summary: Tide two: Reyes's divers blanket the site with sonar buoys, legally fencing the water. Ansel sneaks among them, plants a false marker to misdirect the fleet, and steals a buoy's data log showing Reyes already knows the true coordinates. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by how easily she lies now.

chapters.title: Quist's Offer
chapters.summary: Marlo Quist corners Ansel with a clean offer: sell him the charts, he erases her debt and Ferro's mortgage. He shows her a photograph proving her father died in his custody — an accident, he says, or negligence, depending on her answer. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Middle Tide
chapters.summary: Tide three: Ansel and Ferro reach the wreck itself. Inside the hold, beneath silver ingots, they find sealed ledgers — cargo manifests recording the Chumara laborers transported aboard, names and wages never paid. POV: Ferro. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into horror; the treasure is a crime scene.

chapters.title: What Gold Buys
chapters.summary: Ferro wants to raise the silver quietly and retire; Ansel wants the ledgers made public. Their argument fractures the partnership, and Ferro sails back alone — straight into a harbor patrol tipped off by an anonymous call. POV: Ferro. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the suspicion that Ansel may have made the call herself.

chapters.title: Held at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Ferro is detained on smuggling charges; Mercy is impounded. Ansel realizes Quist orchestrated it to force her hand, and Reyes publicly offers to 'assist' the investigation — buying the narrative before the truth surfaces. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: isolation; every ally is leverage now.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Ansel returns to the cave and finds a second cache: her father's final letter, confessing he forged the permits under coercion and hid the evidence here, hoping someone braver would finish it. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: mourning and absolution tangled together — her father chose her, in the end.

chapters.title: Buying Back Ferro
chapters.summary: Ansel trades Quist a copy of the charts — deliberately incomplete — for Ferro's release and Mercy's papers. Sela calls it cowardice; Ansel calls it buying time. Both know the fleet will find the false coordinates empty within two tides. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the cost of strategy measured in self-respect.

chapters.title: Tide Five, Storm Rising
chapters.summary: A squall compresses the remaining tide windows. Reyes, furious at the empty coordinates, deduces the deception and posts armed watch on the cave. Ansel, Sela, and a handful of Chumara families plan a night approach through the blowhole passage only locals know. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: a community deciding its inheritance is worth the risk.

chapters.title: The Blowhole Run
chapters.summary: In storm dark, the small boats thread the blowhole. Ansel dives the flooded inner chamber to reach the hold while Sela's people hold the surface against Reyes's launch. The ledgers come up; so does a case of the fleet's original fraudulent claim documents, cached by Tomás. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: triumph half-drowned in adrenaline.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Reyes catches them at the cave mouth and offers Ansel everything — debt cleared, her father honored, a share — if the ledgers burn. Ansel refuses; Reyes orders her divers to collapse the blowhole with the boats inside. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: the villain's genuine belief that ownership is salvation.

chapters.title: Cave-In
chapters.summary: The demolition charge goes wrong in the surge, trapping Reyes's own dive team. Ansel goes back under — for the people trying to kill her — and pulls out two divers while the ledgers and claim documents are ferried to safety. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the choice that defines her; justice isn't vengeance.

chapters.title: The Last Tide
chapters.summary: Dawn, tide six: with the permits expiring at noon, Ansel stands before the harbor crowd and reads the manifests aloud — names, wages, the forged signatures, including her father's. Sela corroborates with the recovered documents. The auction collapses; the state freezes the concession pending inquiry. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: vindication that tastes like grief.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Quist is arrested when Ferro's impound records surface; Reyes flees the territory ahead of fraud charges, her fleet seized. The courts grant the Chumara families standing over the wreck as ancestral property. Ansel's debt dies with Quist's empire, and her father's name is cleared in the same breath that indicts him. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: complicated peace.

chapters.title: Odile and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Months later, the community runs the dive site themselves, the ledgers displayed in a museum built from salvage money. Ansel keeps the compass, declines a seat on the new council, and takes Ferro's Mercy out past the reef at slack tide. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet ending — she was never after treasure, only a horizon she could stand on honestly.
